analysis.title: Asia in Focus - China: Property Downturn Deeper Than Previously Anticipated, But Its Growth Drag Should Still Ease Gradually in the Years Ahead
key_insights: China's property downturn is in its sixth year. Most housing activity indicators have been much weaker than GS projected so far in 2026.
The shift from presales to completed-home sales, with stronger project-level fund supervision, implies tighter developer funding and lower property investment over the next few years.
GS estimates the property sector's share of China's real GDP will fall from around 15% now (nearly 30% at the 2010-2021 peak) to around 8% from 2030 onward.

Adding five direct channels (construction, real estate services, upstream commodity demand, move-in consumption, land-sales fiscal effects), GS estimates a 1.8pp drag on real GDP growth in 2026, versus 1.7pp in 2025 and a previous 2026 estimate of 1.5pp.
GS expects the direct drag to narrow by around 0.5pp to 1.3pp in 2027 and largely fade by 2030.

The indirect housing wealth effect amplifies the growth impact and peaked in 2024-25. It should fade in the early 2030s if nationwide existing home prices bottom in 2030, as GS's property research team expects.
The property construction downturn is deeper and more protracted than previously anticipated because the government aims to significantly reduce new home supply.

Top-tier cities such as Shanghai and Shenzhen, where inventory is already low, may see home prices recover soon. Lower-tier cities with large inventory overhang may keep falling for the next few years.
GS's property research team projects a more than 90% decline in residential land sales volume from 2025 to 2035, implying persistent local government financing pressure.

GS sees scope for a nationwide property tax expansion toward the end of the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-30) or during the 16th (2031-35), to broaden the local tax base and partly offset lost land sales revenue.

Technical changes to the model: floor space under construction is re-estimated from new home starts, because stuck projects keep NBS figures from showing the full decline. Land sales revenue now uses the Ministry of Finance series because the NBS stopped publishing developer land-purchase volume.

sector_views.rationale: Activity indicators are down 60-90% from 2020-21 peaks, and policy is cutting new home supply and developer funding. GS expects further declines in starts, sales, investment and land sales through 2027 and beyond.

risk_factors: Developer funding is tighter under the presales-to-completed-sales shift, which may add downward pressure to property indicators.
Local government financing pressure is likely to persist, especially in regions more dependent on property-related revenue, requiring alternative revenue sources or spending cuts.
Lower-tier cities with large inventory overhang may see prices decline for several more years.
The negative housing wealth effect on household confidence and consumption continues until existing home prices bottom, which GS expects in 2030.
